page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-56 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 448 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highmem-56 demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU suites. Memory performance is highly competitive, with Passmark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier and small-block cached read bandwidth exceeding 3.9 TB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. The instance also shows strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, alongside efficient text generation for small and medium LLM models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-56 offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or hardware acceleration. Its high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it well-suited for large-scale database operations, memory-cached web serving, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks. However, the absence of local storage means users must attach external persistent disks, which represents a structural tradeoff for I/O-heavy database applications.
